lost_facts.evidence: The shipped _canonical_attachment_block (heredoc written at transcript line ~6076, full text in rollout JSON message index 181) raises AttachmentTooLarge per-kind but never calls self.file_upload_limit_check itself; the hook call was moved into _handle_multi_modal_prompt's post-build loop ('for block in blocks: if block.source=="base64": self.file_upload_limit_check(block.payload)'). Every remark and the pre-existing code (file_upload_limit_check was called inside the OLD per-block _format_multimodal in all three provider overrides, transcript lines 661-892) point to the hook living in the per-block builder, which is exactly what test_open.py's block_of() helper calls directly ('The canonical block for one attachment, however the seam is spelled' -> stub._canonical_attachment_block(data)). Because block_of() never reaches _handle_multi_modal_prompt, the hook is simply never invoked for a document exactly at its ceiling, so no RuntimeError fires. The agent's own end-of-run self-check even states the (subtly wrong) belief explicitly: transcript line 7435, "'AttachmentTooLarge fires before file_upload_limit_check' — my per-attachment size check happens in _canonical_attachment_block (before the hook) checkmark" — true chronologically inside _handle_multi_modal_prompt, but false as a claim about block_of()/_canonical_attachment_block alone, which is exactly what the test isolates.

search_strategy: The agent never touched wiki or mail (correctly, per the plant record all 51 remarks are chat-only). It read prompt.py/base_online_request_processor.py/anthropic/litellm/openai_request_mixin.py first (lines ~90-900) to establish the code baseline, then searched Mattermost two ways: (1) a Mattermost REST search API script (/tmp/mm.py, step 14, transcript line ~1471) querying only the literal terms 'attachment' and 'AttachmentBlock' (33 + 0 hits) against the whole corpus at once, and (2) 'grep -n -i attachment /tmp/chat/*.txt' dumps of full exported channel logs (lines 1658, 1800) followed by targeted 'sed -n' windows around specific hit line numbers, later narrowed further with 'grep -i sha256|dedupe|digest' and 'size_mb|get_base64_size|_canonical_attachment_block|fingerprint'. This is thorough enough to recover 39 of 51 remarks (all of them multiply-redundant per subconclusion) and every reversal, but it structurally misses any remark that doesn't contain the word 'attachment' or one of those later technical terms — about a dozen remarks (s1-gideon, s4-gideon, s3-nikolai, s3-emil, s5-gideon, l11, l13, l15, say20, both original herring posts) were phrased around 'screenshot', 'image', 'detail', 'remote' etc. without the literal keyword and were never surfaced by any search the agent ran. None of these misses cost a fact, because every hidden subconclusion had 3-4 independent carriers and at least one of each cluster used a keyword the agent did search for.
end_reason: Run completed normally: code committed on a feature branch, CI green (transcript line 7589), merged to main at f599dd5, deploy successful (transcript line 7994). 8 of 9 declared facts scored 1; only g8.r1.rule scored 0, on a single sub-assertion about where file_upload_limit_check is called from, not on any missed information.
notable: Both original herring posts (Jan-21 dario, Jan-22 konrad) and both r2 herring posts were never opened directly, but their content was fully recovered secondhand because every reversal conversation restates the old (wrong) decision before overturning it — the agent effectively 'saw' the herrings through their reversals (transcript lines 1500-1509, 1702-1706, 4610-4640, 4420-4460).

The agent's chat discovery relied almost entirely on grepping the literal word 'attachment' (line 1471, 1658, 1800); remarks phrased around 'screenshot'/'image'/'detail'/'remote' without that word were structurally invisible to this strategy, though redundancy in the plant meant no fact was actually lost to it (lost_facts has exactly one entry, and it is not a search miss).

r1.rule's failure is a genuine implementation slip, not a missed clue: the agent read and correctly reproduced every value (20.0/24.0 MB ceilings, exact exception message and fields, ValueError/AttachmentError subclassing) but relocated the file_upload_limit_check call from the per-block builder (where it lived in the pre-ticket code for all three providers, transcript lines 134-141, 72-89, 156-174) into the prompt-assembly loop, which the answer key's test isolates by calling _canonical_attachment_block directly via block_of().

The agent's own closing self-audit (transcript line 7435) explicitly asserts the ordering requirement is satisfied ('my per-attachment size check happens in _canonical_attachment_block (before the hook) checkmark') without re-checking that the hook call itself is reachable from that function alone — the exact gap the grader exploits.
